class: The same full local gate runs more than once on the same commit (builder, orchestrator, then --pre-push), each taking minutes, and CI then re-runs everything again; the repeats add time and extra chances for a load-related false red without adding evidence.
mechanism: Each role runs the gate on its own because no rule says a builder's GATE PASS <sha> is accepted when the sha equals HEAD. Three runs of about 8-11 min each stack up per change, before CI's own 7.2 min plus 10-16 min runs.

first_seen.where: rows 30-32, audit section 3 items 3-4 and section 5 #4
first_seen.evidence: builder gate + orchestrator gate + --pre-push, about 8-11 min each; gh run list: CI 7.2 min, App tests 9.7-15.6 min; 5 of 10 orchestrator gates failed (about 44 of 93 min); the 30b builder's 10-min gate ran on a tree that had already moved and was thrown away.

fix: ADR-188 (2): one gate per commit. The orchestrator accepts the builder's GATE PASS <sha> when sha = HEAD; --pre-push only if the sha changed. ADR-178 tracker row 15.

detection.note: No check: this is an ADR-188 (2) practice. Tracker row 15 counts gate runs per sha by hand until a script does.

occurrences.evidence: three gate runs per change plus CI (audit section 3 item 4)
